name: edit-straddles-emphasis-start

now: She counted the hulls twice and was quite **tired** by the end of it.

name: edit-straddles-emphasis-end
why: the edit consumes the closing delimiter and the word after it
was: She counted the hulls twice and was **very tired** by the end of it.
now: She counted the hulls twice and was **very** tired indeed by the end of it.

runs.text: She counted the hulls twice and was

name: edit-inside-italic-inside-bold
why: nested inline markup — the boundary lands between two delimiter runs

now: The gulls had stopped, and **that was the *only part* she remembered** afterwards.

now: Maren did not run. <!-- mutate:entity=char-maren;field=mood;value=numb;id=m1 --> She stood where she was.

now: The boats lay <!-- embedded-todo:id=t1;status=open;note=check%20the%20tide -->over on their black sides<!-- /embedded-todo --> like something sleeping.

name: split-shifts-every-later-block
why: a split early in the scene shifts every later block by one, so difflib pairs unrelated paragraphs one-to-one; word-diffing those interleaves them into mush that still reassembles and still renders well-formed (#409)
was:
The tide went out further than she had ever seen it.

She counted the hulls twice. The eleventh was moored at the harbour.

Maren did not run. She had never done the sensible thing quickly.
now:
The tide went out further than she had ever seen it.

She counted the hulls twice.

The eleventh was moored at the harbour.

Maren did not run. She had never done the sensible thing quickly.

runs.text:
The tide went out further than she had ever seen it.

She counted the hulls twice.
The eleventh was moored at the harbour.
The eleventh was moored at the harbour.
Maren did not run. She had never done the sensible thing quickly.

A man who arrives composed has been waiting somewhere nearby.

The door opens before I reach it, and a servant looks at my face.

A man who arrives composed has been waiting somewhere near.

The door opens before I reach it, and a servant looks at my face.

name: rewrite-test-is-symmetric
why: isjunk applies to a matcher's second sequence only, so the rewrite test scored this pair 0.74 one way round and under 0.5 the other; the was-side look-ahead asked it backwards and paired the grown paragraph with its neighbour (#2591)

"Sir." A servant, grey at the temples.

He turns and walks.

Beyond the house is the stable, and beside it a training surround: a ring of peeled poles perhaps 15 meters across, sand footing raked flat. The servant stops at the gate.
now: Beyond the house is the stable, and beside the stable a training surround: a ring of peeled poles 15 meters across, sand raked flat. The servant stops at the gate and tips his chin at the ring and goes back the way he came.
